The issue in [`BaseSecantSolver.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_50_group_a_blind/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math/analysis/solvers/BaseSecantSolver.java#L184-L191) has been investigated and fixed.

### Root Cause
Under `Method.REGULA_FALSI`, an artificial modification to `x0` and `f0` when `x == x1` was interfering with the standard Regula Falsi algorithm contract. By specification and standard behavior, Regula Falsi maintains the unshifted bracket boundary (`case REGULA_FALSI: // Nothing.`), which can legitimately exhaust evaluation limits when stagnation occurs. This caused [`testIssue631`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_50_group_a_blind/src/test/java/org/apache/commons/math/analysis/solvers/RegulaFalsiSolverTest.java#L44-L56) (which expects a `TooManyEvaluationsException`) to fail.

### Solution
Removed the artificial adjustment in [`BaseSecantSolver.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/math_50_group_a_blind/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/math/analysis/solvers/BaseSecantSolver.java#L184-L191), restoring the standard Regula Falsi behavior.
